purpose: Record external design references, original/official sources, verified structural features, rights/licensing boundaries, and the exact Project Intersection reuse decision.

systems.name: Open Research Knowledge Graph (ORKG)
systems.operator: TIB – Leibniz Information Centre for Science and Technology / ORKG project
design_influence: templates that standardize comparable contribution fields
systems.rights_boundary: ORKG architectural concepts are cited as inspiration. Project Intersection does not copy ORKG page text, UI, source code, visual assets, or datasets. If ORKG data is imported later, its then-current data-license/source metadata must be recorded separately.

sources.title: ORKG About — Comparisons and structured research contributions
verified_points: ORKG describes research papers in structured form.
Comparisons organize contributions addressing a research question in a tabular, filterable overview.
Templates are used to specify comparable contribution structures.
sources.rights_note: Used as a factual/design reference only; no page expression copied.

sources.title: ORKG Academy — Template Course
verified_points: Templates provide a skeleton for contribution data structures.
Templates help contributions addressing the same problem conform to a comparable structure.
sources.rights_note: Used as a factual/design reference only; no course text or visual asset copied.

sources.title: FAIR scientific information with the Open Research Knowledge Graph
verified_points: ORKG is described as infrastructure for production, curation, publication, and use of FAIR scientific information.
sources.rights_note: Article is published under CC BY 4.0. Project cites the work; no article text or figures are reproduced.

sources.title: ORKG backend repository
verified_points: The public ORKG backend repository identifies the software license as MIT.
sources.rights_note: Software-license fact recorded only. No ORKG code was copied into Project Intersection.

sources.title: Rethinking the production and publication of machine-readable expressions of research findings
verified_points: The article states that the ORKG data used in its examples are published under CC0 1.0 Universal.
It states that ORKG components are open source under the MIT license.
sources.rights_note: Used to document a reported ORKG data/software licensing boundary. Future ORKG data imports must still verify the current license at import time.

systems.name: Wikidata
systems.rights_boundary: Project Intersection independently implements its own entity/relation schema. No Wikidata UI, item text, or dumps were copied.

sources.title: Wikidata: Data model
verified_points: Wikidata represents knowledge with entities/items and statements.
Statements use a subject/predicate/object-like structure.
Qualifiers can restrict the scope or meaning of statements.

sources.title: Help: Statements
verified_points: Statements can include qualifiers, references, and ranks.

sources.title: Wikidata: Licensing
verified_points: Structured data in the main, Property, Lexeme, and EntitySchema namespaces is released under CC0.
Text in other namespaces is available under CC BY-SA 4.0.
sources.rights_note: License boundary recorded. No Wikidata data is currently bundled.

systems.name: OpenAlex
systems.rights_boundary: OpenAlex data may be reusable under CC0, but Project Intersection currently uses only architecture concepts and does not bundle OpenAlex records.

sources.title: OpenAlex Data reference
verified_points: OpenAlex models works, authors, sources, institutions, publishers, funders, topics, and other entities.
Entities are connected and have OpenAlex IDs.
OpenAlex records can map to external identifiers such as DOI, ORCID, ROR, ISSN, and Wikidata.

sources.title: OpenAlex API reference
verified_points: Entity types are exposed as REST endpoints.
The documentation states that all OpenAlex data is CC0.
sources.rights_note: CC0 data-license fact recorded; no OpenAlex dataset is currently copied.

systems.name: Papers with Code
systems.operator: Community project supported by Meta AI Research
systems.rights_boundary: Papers with Code states that its content/data is CC BY-SA. Project Intersection does not import or adapt that content in v1, avoiding attribution/share-alike obligations for this architecture layer.

sources.title: About Papers With Code
verified_points: Papers with Code organizes papers, code, datasets, methods, and evaluation tables.
It states that website content/data is licensed under CC BY-SA.
Benchmark results and community contribution workflows are core features.
sources.rights_note: Only the general architecture idea is referenced; no PWC content/data is copied.

sources.title: Papers with Code Dataset Licensing Guide
verified_points: The guide warns that an indexed dataset's license may differ from code or annotation licenses.
It emphasizes checking the actual dataset license and ownership.
sources.rights_note: Used as a rights-handling precedent, not as a license for third-party datasets.

systems.name: MITRE ATT&CK®
design_influence: linking abstract categories to observed procedures
systems.rights_boundary: Project Intersection does not copy ATT&CK content, matrices, technique descriptions, IDs, logos, or branding. The term is used only to identify a design reference. Any future ATT&CK content reuse must reproduce MITRE's required copyright/license notice and comply with trademark rules.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK Get Started
verified_points: ATT&CK is a knowledge base of adversary techniques based on real-world observations.
Its model distinguishes tactics, techniques, sub-techniques, and procedures.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK Terms of Use
verified_points: MITRE grants a non-exclusive, royalty-free license for research, development, and commercial use.
Copies must reproduce MITRE's copyright designation and the license notice.
sources.rights_note: No ATT&CK content is currently copied, so the Project does not rely on this license for bundled material.

sources.title: MITRE ATT&CK Legal & Branding
verified_points: MITRE ATT&CK and ATT&CK are registered trademarks.
Use must not imply MITRE sponsorship or endorsement.
ATT&CK must not be used as a Project product/service/brand name.
sources.rights_note: Project uses MITRE ATT&CK only as a cited external reference.

project_design_mapping.independent_project_difference: Project adds explicit evidence-class boundaries, failure/correction lineage, and claim-status transitions.

project_design_mapping.project_feature: qualified relation with scope + evidence_class + source_path
project_design_mapping.independent_project_difference: Qualifiers are specialized for scientific-evidence scope and Project provenance.
IDs encode Project object classes such as RQ, CL, EX, EV, FR, CR, PA, HC, NC.

project_design_mapping.project_feature: failure/mechanism matrix and traversable taxonomy direction
project_design_mapping.independent_project_difference: Project failure objects concern research/governance failure modes, not cyber-adversary techniques.
